# pg_corpus_edge.txt -- surface S4 (polymap ipart/fpart edge walk)
#
# FROZEN FIXTURE.  Generated by pg_mkcorpus.py.
#
# GRAMMAR:  EDGE <id> n= mp=x0,y0;... miny= maxy=
#
# ipart[] is the LEFT boundary (seeded ubxl=311); fpart[] is the RIGHT
# boundary (seeded lbxl=5).  TDPOLYGS.H:2539.  The names are inverted
# relative to the obvious reading.
#
# miny/maxy are PINNED inputs, not recomputed from mp[].  In polymap they
# come from the projector's y-only extent after the two normalisation
# steps at :2487-2499, which is a different quantity from min(mp.y).

EDGE ED_TRI n=3 mp=50,30;200,60;120,150 miny=30 maxy=150
EDGE ED_QUAD n=4 mp=50,30;200,40;210,150;40,140 miny=30 maxy=150
EDGE ED_ABOVE_TOP n=3 mp=50,-40;200,-30;120,150 miny=10 maxy=150
EDGE ED_CROSS_TOP n=3 mp=50,-5;200,20;120,150 miny=10 maxy=150
EDGE ED_CROSS_BOT n=3 mp=50,30;200,60;120,260 miny=30 maxy=190
EDGE ED_BOTH n=3 mp=50,-100;200,-90;120,400 miny=10 maxy=190
EDGE ED_ONESCAN n=3 mp=50,100;200,101;120,101 miny=100 maxy=101
EDGE ED_HORIZ n=3 mp=50,100;200,100;120,150 miny=100 maxy=150
EDGE ED_TALL n=3 mp=60,10;70,190;200,100 miny=10 maxy=190
EDGE ED_CLAMP_LEFT n=3 mp=-40000,50;200,60;120,150 miny=50 maxy=150
EDGE ED_CLAMP_RIGHT n=3 mp=40000,50;200,60;120,150 miny=50 maxy=150
# bndx landing exactly on k+0.5 at every scanline: dx/dy = 1/2 with an
# odd start, so the accumulator alternates .0 and .5.  This is the
# nearest-even site a truncating port gets wrong.
EDGE ED_TIE_HALF n=3 mp=51,20;101,120;60,120 miny=20 maxy=120
EDGE ED_TIE_HALF2 n=3 mp=50,20;100,120;61,120 miny=20 maxy=120
# quarter steps: .25/.5/.75 sequence, only one of four rows is a tie
EDGE ED_TIE_QTR n=3 mp=50,20;75,120;60,120 miny=20 maxy=120
# negative slope, so a truncating port biases the other way
EDGE ED_NEG_SLOPE n=3 mp=200,20;150,120;210,120 miny=20 maxy=120
# long edge: 170 scanlines of accumulator drift
EDGE ED_DRIFT n=3 mp=20,10;300,180;25,180 miny=10 maxy=180
EDGE ED_DRIFT_REV n=3 mp=300,10;20,180;295,180 miny=10 maxy=180
# mp[] above 2**24, as a blown-up near-plane interpolation produces
EDGE ED_HUGE n=3 mp=20000000,50;200,60;120,150 miny=50 maxy=150
# ity == jty exactly, reachable only through the top clip: an edge from
# y=5 to y=10 has ity=lbyl=10 and jty=10, and `jnl noifor` (ity>=jty)
# makes it contribute NOTHING.  The source comment says h<=jty; the code
# says otherwise.
EDGE ED_ITY_EQ_JTY n=3 mp=60,5;120,10;200,60 miny=10 maxy=60
# ED_ITY_EQ_JTY only moves the record if the skipped edge would have
# contributed a value no OTHER edge already covers.  When the edge ends
# on a shared vertex at y=lbyl the next edge starts from the same x, so
# the write is absorbed.  Here BOTH edges incident on the y=10 vertex
# come from above it, so both are skipped and row 10 keeps its seeds
# (ipart=311, fpart=5, an empty span).  `<=` would fill it with 160:160
# and the polygon would stop vanishing.
EDGE ED_ITY_EQ_JTY2 n=3 mp=20,2;300,2;160,10 miny=10 maxy=20
# top clip landing on an exact half: kx = 5/20 = 0.25 exactly, so
# (lbyl-y1)*kx = 10*0.25 = 2.5 exactly and x1 = 51 is ODD.  Rounding the
# SUM gives rne(53.5) = 54; rounding the PRODUCT first gives 51+2 = 53.
# This single row is what separates the two.
EDGE ED_TIE_TOPCLIP n=3 mp=51,0;56,20;200,100 miny=10 maxy=100
EDGE ED_TIE_TOPCLIP2 n=3 mp=53,0;58,20;200,100 miny=10 maxy=100
# closing edge mp[vr22] = mp[0] must be walked too
EDGE ED_CLOSING n=3 mp=200,30;210,150;50,60 miny=30 maxy=150
